NSDHL dysfunction causes the developmental syndrome that includes ipsilateral body hypoplasia. The intervening tissue-specific processes are unresolved; this edge does not assign the phenotype to a demonstrated Hedgehog or clone-clearance pathway.

NSDHL dysfunction underlies the limb-reduction phenotype through incompletely resolved developmental processes. A specific Hedgehog-mediated route in human limbs is not established by the mouse neural-culture experiments.
The biosynthetic defect can reduce cholesterol availability within affected cells.
Intermediates upstream of the enzymatic block accumulate.
Cultured granule-cell experiments support impaired reception of SHH when cholesterol is limiting.

Reduced availability of a barrier lipid is proposed to contribute to the abnormal secretory apparatus; patient ultrastructure and treatment response do not isolate this contribution from precursor effects.
Precursor-associated toxicity is a proposed contributor to the secretory abnormality in patient skin; the specific responsible sterols and intermediate steps remain unresolved.
Age-dependent changes in mutant-cell representation occur in mosaic mouse tissues, with differential proliferation and survival unresolved.
The patient expression and biopsy findings associate mutant-expressing epidermis with the secretory lesion; the lineage and selection mechanisms producing the distribution remain unresolved.
Functional mosaicism contributes to the distribution of affected skin. The developmental steps producing a sharp body-midline boundary remain unknown, and bilateral patterns can occur.

Accelerated receptor degradation can reduce the signaling receptor pool; mouse-skin observations support reduced pathway activation in NSDHL-null regions.
Defective follicle growth in Nsdhl mouse skin is consistent with the human failure of hair growth; the intervening human pathway has not been demonstrated.

nodes.description: Topical lovastatin or simvastatin combined with cholesterol has improved cutaneous lesions in uncontrolled reports. Skin improvement does not establish correction of congenital skeletal defects, and long-term comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

evidence.snippet: Herein, we report a case of successful treatment of the cutaneous features of CHILD syndrome with compounded simvastatin and cholesterol gel and highlight the role of the compounding pharmacist in the care of patients with congenital ichthyosis.

nodes.description: X-inactivation creates functional mosaicism in heterozygous females. In one patient, cultured keratinocytes from affected and unaffected skin expressed different NSDHL alleles, while affected fibroblasts retained both. These observations do not explain the precise midline boundary or demonstrate longitudinal cell clearance.
